subject: Startups
title: Gross Burn vs. Net Burn
description: A micro-lesson that makes Gross Burn vs. Net Burn usable.

hook.text: Two startups both burn $500K per month. One earns nothing. The other earns $400K. Same burn, different realities.

buildup.text: Gross burn is total monthly spending. Net burn is spending minus revenue. Net burn is what actually drains cash.

discovery.text: Investors care about net burn because it determines the true runway. A company earning revenue burns less cash.

twist.text: A startup can increase gross burn (hiring more) while decreasing net burn (earning more). That's healthy growth.

climax.text: When net burn hits zero, you're break-even. Below zero, you're profitable. No longer depending on investors.

punchline.text: Gross burn is spending. Net burn is what matters.

quiz.question: What is the difference between gross burn and net burn?
options: Net burn subtracts revenue from total spending
